summary: Environment-topology tool pack: what a deployment target actually holds, and what it must never hold. Both tools are offline — no network, no credential, no subprocess. wrangler-env-lint.py names every binding and var a named Wrangler environment silently loses: Cloudflare documents bindings and environment variables as non-inheritable, so vars, kv_namespaces, d1_databases, r2_buckets, durable_objects, queues, services and secrets do not reach [env.production] from the top level while routes and workers_dev do, and the failure surfaces only as an undefined in production at request time. It also reports an unset compatibility_date and a durable object class bound without a migration that creates it, parses JSONC with its own string-aware comment and trailing-comma stripper because the standard library has none, and reads wrangler.toml through tomllib. secret-leak-scan.py finds committed credentials in a worktree, its CI config and optionally its built output — Supabase sb_secret_ keys and legacy service_role JWTs, decoded to read the role claim rather than pattern-matched because the publishable half of the legacy pair is the same shape and is meant to ship, Cloudflare cfut_ tokens, private key blocks, high-entropy assignments and a real .env that .gitignore does not cover — and never prints a secret: a finding is file:line, the rule, the severity and at most the first 8 characters. It scans the worktree only, deliberately not git history.
